subject: Question about pairwise analysis for univariate data

messages.author: 443521c17f5ceeb4
messages.subject: Question about pairwise analysis for univariate data
parts:
Hello all,

My question relates purely to the RRPP package rather than geomorph, I hope that isn't a problem!

I have been using the RRPP package to run a phylogenetic ANOVA on my data, using the model:

Fullmod <- lm.rrpp(R1 ~ E1 + E2 + E3 + E4, data = Data, print.progress = T, Cov = Finalvcv,  RRPP = T, SS.type = "II", iter = 999999)

Where R1 is our univariate response variable (an average value recorded for each species) and E1-E4 are explanatory environmental variables.

When I run the model, E1 has a significant effect (r^2 = 0.44, F = 12.1, p < 0.0001). From plotting the data, it seems likely that one particular category in E1 is very distinct, and likely driving this pattern.

However, when I run a pairwise analysis to look for differences in means between groups, using:

PW <- pairwise(Fullmod, groups = Data$E1)
summary(PW, confidence = 0.95, test.type = "dist")

No pairwise difference is significant, and we get very high p-values, even between groups with very different R1 values.

Is the pairwise test I am using appropriate? Or is there some other reason why the pairwise test is not detecting differences between groups? 

I notice in this thread, it is mentioned that there could be a conceptual issue with using RRPP pairwise test to analyse univariate data. Could this be causing the issue?

Thanks for all your help,

Edd Page

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Question about pairwise analysis for univariate data
parts:
Dear Edd,

I think with your example, I would need to maybe see the data to see if there is an issue, rather than speculate causes.  If you do not mind sharing (if it is small enough to send), you could send it to me directly outside of the googlegroup and I can take a look.

Here are some other things to try to see if you get different answers, to help elucidate if this might be a bug:

1. Try different types of SS and see if the result changes much.
2. Try without the covariance matrix and see if the result makes more sense.
3. Append a column of 0s to R1, e.g., R2 <- cbind(R1, 0), and replace this matrix for R1 in the analysis.

Option 3 might not surprise me as we just had issues with single variables and R losing names when coercing vectors into matrices or vice versa.  By forcing a matrix, you should get the same ANOVA results but if the pairwise results suddenly make sense, then it might be an indexing problem caused by lost names affecting your pairwise results.

Regardless, I am happy to take a look if you are willing to share data.

Cheers!
Mike
